summary: LinkedIn OAuth for an AI agent is self-serve if you stay within the open consumer scopes: sign in/profile/email and Share on LinkedIn. The catch is that the open set is small, redirect URLs must match exactly, and broader profile editing or marketing/community-management access needs separate approval or is closed.
difficultyReason: The core setup is self-serve in the Developer Portal and the open consumer permissions are available without special approval. The main limitation is scope: the agent can sign in, read basic profile/email, and post/comment/like, but more advanced write or partner APIs move you into reviewed programs.

timeToProduction.text: Same day for open consumer scopes; longer if you need Page-association approval or any partner-program review.

requirements.text: Create the app in LinkedIn Developer Portal with an app name, LinkedIn Page, privacy policy URL, and logo.
requirements.quote: In the Privacy policy URL box, enter your privacy policy URL.

requirements.text: Associate the app with a LinkedIn Page; apps stay tied to that Page.
requirements.quote: Apps are permanently associated with a specific LinkedIn Page and cannot be transferred to another page.

requirements.text: Add the exact HTTPS redirect URI you use in Composio; it must match one of the app's Redirect URLs.
requirements.quote: This value must match one of the Redirect URLs defined in your application configuration.

requirements.text: Use the OpenID Connect product for sign-in scopes; LinkedIn now uses openid, profile, and email.
requirements.quote: We are also introducing new scopes `profile` and `email`.

requirements.text: Use Share on LinkedIn for posting/commenting/liking on behalf of the member.
requirements.quote: make sure to request the `w_member_social` scope!

requirements.text: If you change scopes later, make users re-authenticate.
requirements.quote: If the `scope` permissions are changed in your app, your users must re-authenticate

requirements.text: Plan for LinkedIn's sign-in/userinfo daily rate limits.
Plan for LinkedIn's share API daily rate limits.

reviewTriggers.quote: Developers seeking to build a marketing related integration using Advertising API permissions must be approved.

reviewTriggers.quote: Developers seeking to build sales related integration using one of the permissions below must be approved as a Sales Navigator Application Platform (SNAP) partner.

reviewTriggers.text: Talent integrations require applying to the specific program.
reviewTriggers.quote: Developers seeking to build talent related integrations through one of the programs listed below can apply here.

reviewTriggers.text: Compliance access is closed and may not be requested.
reviewTriggers.quote: Access is closed and may not be requested.

reviewTriggers.quote: The use of this API is restricted to those developers approved by LinkedIn.

steps.title: Create or confirm your LinkedIn Page
steps.detail: If you do not already have one, create a LinkedIn Page first; some products require it and the app is tied to that Page.
steps.quote: For certain functionality and products, you're required to associate your app with a LinkedIn Page.

steps.title: Create the app in the Developer Portal
steps.detail: Go to My Apps > Create app, enter the app name, LinkedIn Page, privacy policy URL, and logo, then accept the terms.
steps.quote: Click My apps in the upper-right corner of the page.

steps.title: Add the Composio redirect URL
steps.detail: On the Auth tab, add the exact HTTPS redirect URL shown in your Composio auth config.
steps.quote: Add the redirect (callback) URL via `HTTPS` to your server.

steps.title: Enable the products you need
steps.detail: Request Sign in with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect and Share on LinkedIn in the Products tab.
steps.quote: The following permissions are available to all developers, and may be added via self-service through the LinkedIn Developer Portal

steps.title: Copy your app credentials
steps.detail: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from the Auth tab and store them securely.
steps.quote: Do not share your Client Secret value with anyone

steps.title: Request the minimum scopes
steps.detail: Use openid, profile, email, and w_member_social for login plus posting/commenting/liking, and avoid extra scopes you cannot justify.
steps.quote: Use the OpenID scope `openid` to get the ID Token.

steps.title: Member authorizes the app
steps.detail: The user signs in, approves the consent screen, and LinkedIn returns an authorization code.
steps.quote: The code is a value that you exchange with LinkedIn for an OAuth 2.0 access token

steps.title: Exchange the code for tokens
steps.detail: Swap the code for an access token, then store the token and build for reauth before expiry.
steps.quote: To protect members' data, LinkedIn does not generate long-lived access tokens.

steps.title: Test identity read and posting
steps.detail: Verify the grant by calling the profile/userinfo endpoint and a small post flow before exposing it to users.

blockers.problem: LinkedIn does not expose a general self-serve profile-edit permission.
blockers.whatToDo: Limit the product to sign-in plus posting/commenting/liking, or apply for the restricted profile-edit path if your use case truly needs it.
blockers.quote: The use of this API is restricted to those developers approved by LinkedIn.

blockers.problem: Programmatic refresh tokens are not broadly available.
blockers.whatToDo: Assume you will need a re-authentication flow when the 60-day access token expires unless LinkedIn enables refresh tokens for your app.
blockers.quote: Programmatic refresh tokens are available for a limited set of partners.

agentDrafts.title: App description
agentDrafts.text: AI assistant that lets a LinkedIn member sign in, read basic profile and email data for identity, and create posts or engage with posts on their behalf after explicit consent.

agentDrafts.title: Why we request openid, profile, and email
agentDrafts.text: We use these scopes only to authenticate the member and retrieve the basic profile and email needed to identify the connected account and personalize the experience.

agentDrafts.title: Why we request w_member_social
agentDrafts.text: We use this scope so the member can ask the assistant to create posts, comments, or likes on LinkedIn after the member explicitly approves the action.

openQuestions: Does your agent need anything beyond basic profile/email and post/comment/like? I could not confirm a public self-serve scope for general member editing or direct messages.
Do you want to use only the Composio managed app first, or do you need your own LinkedIn app immediately for branding and custom scopes?
LinkedIn's public docs I checked did not publish a fee for the open consumer scopes.
